EPIRB (Emergency Position-Indicating Rad: The EPIRB (Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon) is a radio beacon with its own battery that sends a search and rescue alert via Cospas-Sarsat in grave and imminent danger. The 406–406.1 MHz digital distress message carries the 15-character HEX identity and, if available, the GNSS position. The chain satellite → LUT (Local User Terminal) → MCC (Mission Control Centre) → RCC/MRCC → SAR craft operates. 121.5 MHz is for local homing/direction finding by suitable SAR craft; since 2009 Cospas-Sarsat satellites have not processed 121.5 MHz distress alerts.

The EPIRB (Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon) is a position-indicating beacon with its own battery that sends a 406 MHz satellite distress message in grave and imminent danger such as abandoning ship or sinking. To use it technically correctly, the 406 MHz alert, 121.5 MHz homing, the new-generation AIS position transmission, the HRU/water sensor distinction, the test procedure and the radar-SART display must be kept apart. This training aims to enable the officer to check the beacon on board.
EPIRB → Cospas-Sarsat uydu faydalı yükü: EPIRB → Cospas-Sarsat satellite payload (LEOSAR, GEOSAR, MEOSAR) → ground terminal LUT (Local User Terminal) → MCC (Mission Control Centre) → the relevant RCC/MRCC (Rescue Coordination Centre) → search and rescue units. 'The signal goes to the satellite' describes only the first step of this chain.
EPIRB ile karşı tarafa sesli yanıt gönde: You cannot send a voice reply with an EPIRB; the RCC receiving the alert does not mean that every ship at sea detects you directly. With an AIS-EPIRB, local visibility depends on range and the AIS receiver/overlay status.
EPIRB kayıt bilgisi, onaylı bakım belges: The EPIRB registration details, approved maintenance document, last self-test, battery and HRU expiry dates and the HEX ID on the beacon label must match the records on board.
EPIRB onaylı float-free braketinde dış g: The EPIRB is stowed on the open deck in its approved float-free bracket. As the ship sinks, the hydrostatic pressure opens the Hydrostatic Release Unit (HRU) mechanism at about 1–4 m depending on the model. The beacon is released mechanically and floats to the surface; when the water sensor/electrodes get wet, the electronic circuit starts the transmission.
EPIRB radarda 12 nokta üretmez; radar-SA: An EPIRB does not produce 12 dots on radar; a radar-SART does, and an AIS-EPIRB may appear on the AIS display.
EPIRB self-test yapmak isterken yanlışlı: While trying to carry out an EPIRB self-test, ON/DISTRESS was activated by mistake. What should be done?
EPIRB, 406 MHz sayısal imdat alarmını Co: The EPIRB delivers a 406 MHz digital distress alert via Cospas-Sarsat to the RCC/MRCC. The operating frequencies and display presentations of the radar-SART, AIS-SART and AIS-EPIRB are different. This section teaches how the approved beacon is operated, tested and how its maintenance is tracked in real shipboard conditions.
EPIRB, çalışır durumdaki DSC, sesli MAYD: The EPIRB is not considered the only means of communication replacing a working DSC, voice MAYDAY and other GMDSS methods. In real distress, complementary distress means are used according to the ship's SMS and the Master's orders.
EPIRB, gemi radarına doğrudan hedef çize: An EPIRB is not a device that draws a target directly on the ship's radar; its primary function is to deliver a satellite distress alert to the SAR authority.
EPIRB'nin 121.5 MHz yayını ile 406 MHz y: What is the basic difference between an EPIRB's 121.5 MHz transmission and its 406 MHz transmission?
EPIRB'nin buoyant lanyard'ı gemiye ya da: The EPIRB's buoyant lanyard is not tied to the ship or to the float-free bracket; when necessary it can be attached to a survival craft or a person.
Float-free braketin HRU (Hydrostatic Rel: The HRU (Hydrostatic Release Unit) mechanism of the float-free bracket releases the beacon by pressure as the ship sinks, at about 1–4 m (depending on the model). The water sensor of the beacon that floats to the surface switches on the electronic circuit. The battery is not activated by seawater and does not generate energy from it: a sealed battery is already fitted. The front of the bracket must not be obstructed and the lanyard must not be tied to the ship; manual ON/DISTRESS is used according to the model manual when necessary.
Float-free EPIRB, serbest yüzmesine enge: A float-free EPIRB sits in an approved bracket so that nothing obstructs it from floating free. As the ship sinks, the HRU releases the beacon mechanically by hydrostatic pressure at a depth of about 1–4 m; the beacon floats to the surface and the water sensor activates the electronics. Seawater does not charge the battery or generate power; the beacon's pre-installed battery supplies the energy. Do not tie the lanyard to the ship or the bracket. IMO MSC.471(101) covers the relevant installations from 1 July 2022; it defines requirements such as a battery capacity of at least 48 hours, GNSS, 121.5 MHz and AIS locating. The standards for earlier installations may differ. Check the battery and HRU expiry dates on the actual label; do not apply a fixed 2/5 years to all models. Annual test: MSC.1/Circ.1040/Rev.2. Approved shore-based maintenance at intervals set by the flag and not exceeding 5 years: MSC.1/Circ.1039/Rev.1. Compare the current EPIRB 15 HEX ID registration with the flag/authority records.

Report the beacon HEX ID, position, time of activation and false alert details. Just switching it off is not enough; the satellite alert may already have entered the SAR system.
Gerçek tehlike olmadığını doğrula ve yay: Confirm that there is no real distress and switch off the transmission immediately.
Gerçek tehlikede manuel aktivasyon üreti: In real distress, manual activation is carried out with the manufacturer's two-step safe sequence. On the sea surface the antenna must stay upright with a clear view of the sky. In the liferaft/lifeboat, check the beacon's indicator/light; do not keep the antenna under metal and do not tie the beacon to the sinking ship.

HEX ID, mevki ve zamanı belirterek en ya: Report the false alert to the nearest RCC/MRCC, stating the HEX ID, position and time.

IMO MSC.1/Circ.1039/Rev.1 kapsamında yet: Under IMO MSC.1/Circ.1039/Rev.1, authorised shore-based maintenance is carried out at intervals set by the flag Administration and not exceeding 5 years. The HRU should not be fixed as 'always two years' or the EPIRB battery as 'always five years': the actual label, the approved product and the manufacturer's instructions are the basis.
IMO MSC.1/Circ.1040/Rev.2'nin yıllık tes: The annual test guidance of IMO MSC.1/Circ.1040/Rev.2 covers the physical condition, verification of registration, battery/HRU expiry dates, the 406 MHz self-test and, where possible, verification of the 121.5 MHz and AIS outputs, and bracket and label checks. A routine self-test in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions on board is not the same as the annual survey/test.
IMO MSC.471(101) kapsamında yeni standar: Under IMO MSC.471(101), the battery of an EPIRB subject to the new standard has an operating capacity of at least 48 hours. For real endurance, the battery expiry date, the beacon model and the service conditions are checked. Only the manufacturer's SELF-TEST function is used for testing: visual/label/HRU/expiry check → special TEST mode → check of the LED/error code → correct placement → GMDSS/PMS record. The self-test may make a short, specially coded RF test transmission but must not be a normal distress alert. Switching on ON/DISTRESS for a routine test can create a false SAR alert. On some models the GNSS self-test is separate and can drain the battery; the manufacturer's interval must be followed.
IMO MSC.471(101), ilgili EPIRB'nin batar: IMO MSC.471(101) requires the battery of the relevant EPIRB to have sufficient capacity to operate the beacon for at least 48 hours. This is a minimum performance requirement for the approved type. It cannot be read as a guarantee for a battery that is expired, damaged or unsuitable; the manufacturer's model label and flag requirements are taken into account.
İlgili standart −20°C ile +55°C işletim: The relevant standard includes requirements such as an operating temperature range of −20°C to +55°C, floating upright in water, a locating light visible at night and automatic float-free release before reaching a depth of 4 m.
Kendi geminin EPIRB modelindeki TEST pro: Apply the TEST procedure for your own ship's EPIRB model correctly.
Klasik 406 MHz EPIRB radarın X-band/S-ba: A conventional 406 MHz EPIRB does not create 12 dots on the X-band/S-band radar display. This characteristic presentation belongs to the radar-SART, which responds to 9 GHz X-band radar interrogation; 12 dots may be seen at a distance and arcs at close range. S-band radar does not trigger this response. An AIS-SART shows a special search and rescue target on a suitable AIS/ECDIS. An EPIRB with AIS can also make a local AIS position transmission; its appearing on the radar display with AIS overlay does not mean it is a real radar-SART response. Reception/antenna height, coverage and model requirements differ for each device. Do not teach a range advantage as a universal certainty.
Klasik 406 MHz EPIRB, ne X-band ne S-ban: A conventional 406 MHz EPIRB produces '12 dots' on neither X-band nor S-band radar. A radar-SART, on the other hand, responds to 9 GHz X-band radar pulses; typically 12 successive dots are seen on the radar display, and at close range the image may turn into arcs. S-band radar does not trigger a radar-SART in this way.
Logbook/PMS kaydını tamamlayıp tekrar ak: Complete the logbook/PMS entry and check whether reactivation/service is required.
Master gemiyi terk emri veriyor. Mümkün: The Master gives the order to abandon ship. As far as possible and safe, carry out distress communications by DSC and voice MAYDAY. The assigned person operates the EPIRB according to the manufacturer's instructions or makes sure the automatic float-free arrangement works unobstructed. The beacon's antenna stays facing the open sky; check the active indicator in the liferaft/lifeboat. Do not tie the EPIRB to the sinking ship.
MSC.471(101) kapsamında aktivasyondan so: Under MSC.471(101), after activation the GNSS position must be updated at intervals of not more than five minutes. However, because of satellite geometry, the antenna's view of the sky and processing conditions, an exact and immediate position is not guaranteed for every alert.
MSC.471(101) standardına tabi cihazın ya: On a beacon subject to the MSC.471(101) standard, merely removing it from the bracket by hand must not start a distress alert automatically. An older model may work differently: always follow the beacon's manual.
Onaylı self-test modunda özel formatlı k: In the approved self-test mode there may be a short, specially formatted RF test transmission; the statement 'it sends no RF signal at all' would be technically wrong. The test message is not processed by the satellite system as a real distress alert. However, switching the normal ON/DISTRESS mode on and off is not a routine check; even a single live transmission can lead to a SAR alert.
Pil deniz suyuyla güç üreten veya suyla: The battery is not a battery that generates power from seawater or is charged by water. The electrical energy comes from the pre-installed primary battery in the sealed housing; the water sensor only has a triggering function. Some brackets have a magnet/reed switch combination that detects the beacon being put back, and incorrect mounting can cause a false activation.

The beacon not appearing on AIS does not mean that it is not sending a 406 MHz alert to the SAR satellite.
Yeni performans standardına tabi AIS-EPI: An AIS-EPIRB subject to the new performance standard helps AIS receivers within VHF line of sight by transmitting its position and information such as EPIRB ACTIVE on the AIS 1 (161.975 MHz) and AIS 2 (162.025 MHz) channels. Not all older 406 MHz EPIRB models have the AIS feature. Satellite processing of alerts on the 121.5/243 MHz signals ended on 1 February 2009.
Yeni standarda tabi AIS-EPIRB cihazları,: AIS-EPIRBs subject to the new standard can send an EPIRB ACTIVE position signal to nearby AIS receivers on 161.975 MHz (AIS 1) and 162.025 MHz (AIS 2). Not all older EPIRBs have AIS. A conventional EPIRB does not create the 12 dots of a radar-SART on the X-band/S-band radar display. A radar-SART responding to 9 GHz X-band radar pulses produces a 12-dot series/arcs; an AIS-EPIRB or AIS-SART appears on a suitable AIS/ECDIS display.

Battery and HRU replacement depends on the actual beacon label/manufacturer's instructions. The official registration with the 15 HEX ID must be up to date. In a false alert, the beacon is switched OFF immediately and the identity, position, time and false alert notification are given to the nearest RCC/MRCC.

EPIRB — THE DISTRESS ALERT CHAIN An Emer: EPIRB — THE DISTRESS ALERT CHAIN An Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon (EPIRB) broadcasts a digital distress signal in the 406–406.1 MHz band. The beacon transmits its unique 15-character HEX ID and, where available, GNSS position. Cospas-Sarsat satellites (LEOSAR, GEOSAR, MEOSAR) relay the alert to a Local User Terminal (LUT), Mission Control Centre (MCC), then the appropriate RCC/MRCC, which coordinates SAR resources. EPIRB is not a two-way VHF voice radio or an automatic marine radar target.

The buoyant beacon rises and the water sensor activates its electronics. Seawater does NOT charge or power the battery; a pre-installed sealed battery provides the electrical energy. The beacon can also be activated manually according to its model's instructions. Never tie the buoyant lanyard to the sinking ship. GMDSS dört deniz alanı tanımlar ve her a: GMDSS defines four sea areas, and each area is determined by the infrastructure technology that provides its coverage. Sea area A1 is the area within the DSC (Digital Selective Calling) coverage of at least one VHF coast station; its typical range is 20–30 nautical miles. Sea area A2 is the area outside A1 but within the DSC coverage of an MF (Medium Frequency) coast station; its range typically extends to about 100–150 nautical miles. Under the GMDSS definitions in force from 1 January 2024, A3 is the coverage area, outside A1/A2, in which the ship earth station carried on board, of an IMO-recognized mobile satellite service (RMSS), can provide continuous distress alerting. Inmarsat and Iridium are examples of recognized services; A3 coverage varies with the approved terminal the ship carries. A4 is the area outside A1, A2 and A3 for the ship concerned and does not mean only the polar regions.
Geminin seyir planına dahil olan deniz a: The sea areas included in the ship's passage plan determine the minimum set of equipment it must carry. Equipment common to all areas: VHF-DSC radio, NAVTEX receiver, EPIRB (406 MHz), SART or AIS-SART, and portable VHF sets (at least 2 or 3). Ships going outside A1 must additionally carry an MF-DSC radio. For ships going outside A2, the RMSS ship earth station, MF/HF-DSC equipment and secondary means of alerting to be carried for A3 or A4 are determined from the current SOLAS Chapter IV requirements and the ship's approved radio equipment record. HF-DSC capability is particularly important for A4 requirements; however, the combination chosen must be verified against the ship's certificate. The equipment combination is detailed according to flag State approval, ship type and tonnage. All commercial ships of 300 GT and above on international voyages must be GMDSS-compliant.

During an abandon-ship drill, the SART i: During an abandon-ship drill, the SART is located but nobody can explain its deployment and activation.

A 15 ppm bilge alarm and stopping device: A 15 ppm bilge alarm and stopping device are part of an approved oily-water separation arrangement, but equipment approval never overrides MARPOL discharge conditions or local restrictions.
A 4–20 mA live-zero loop represents zero: A 4–20 mA live-zero loop represents zero span at 4 mA and full span at 20 mA. Current below normal range may indicate a fault; transmitter scaling and loop wiring must be verified.
A bill of lading may evidence receipt, c: A bill of lading may evidence receipt, contract terms and title-related rights. The person signing must be authorised and must not knowingly certify an inaccurate cargo description or condition.
A Bourdon gauge measures pressure throug: A Bourdon gauge measures pressure through elastic tube deformation; piezoelectric sensors are generally suited to dynamic pressure measurement and typically require conditioning. A displayed 0 bar may reflect failed instrumentation rather than zero line pressure.
A cold-front passage can involve rapid w: A cold-front passage can involve rapid wind veer/backing, pressure changes and convective weather; warm fronts often bring more layered cloud and extensive precipitation. Actual weather depends on the system and locality.
A dedicated lookout supports detection b: A dedicated lookout supports detection by sight and hearing under Rule 5 and must report changes clearly; helm, chart and radar duties can impede an effective lookout when workload rises.
A draft survey derives displacement chan: A draft survey derives displacement changes from corrected drafts and hydrostatics, then adjusts for non-cargo weights such as ballast, freshwater, fuel and stores. Water density changes the interpretation of tabulated displacement.
A drill is meaningful when crew actions,: A drill is meaningful when crew actions, timing, communication, access and equipment limitations are observed. Completion of a checklist is not evidence that the response would work under real failure conditions.
A final departure stability check must u: A final departure stability check must use actual cargo, fuel, water, ballast, free-surface states and shipboard draughts. A previously approved loadcase can become invalid after any substantial late shift of a high or longitudinally displaced weight.
A fixed CO₂ installation suppresses fire: A fixed CO₂ installation suppresses fire by displacing oxygen and can be lethal to anyone in the protected space. Release decisions require proper command, evacuation checks and strict access control.
A lifeboat is a survival craft, while a: A lifeboat is a survival craft, while a rescue boat is intended for recovering persons and marshalling survival craft; some installations may meet both roles. Launching procedures are equipment-specific and require trained crew.
A longitudinal moment moves the vessel a: A longitudinal moment moves the vessel away from its initial trim and can be estimated using MCT 1 cm when the loading instrument's assumptions are respected. Signs and draft distribution require LCF and vessel-specific data.
A meridian altitude of the Sun can suppo: A meridian altitude of the Sun can support latitude estimation using corrected noon altitude and the Sun's declination, with hemisphere and zenith-side interpretation required. This is a simplified navigation-school geometry case.
A rhumb line crosses all meridians at a: A rhumb line crosses all meridians at a constant true bearing, appearing straight on a Mercator chart. It does not generally provide the shortest spherical route, especially on long ocean passages at higher latitude.
A running fix transfers an earlier posit: A running fix transfers an earlier position line to the time of a second observation using estimated course, speed and set/drift. Both fixes and transfer errors affect reliability.
A tensioned mooring line stores energy t: A tensioned mooring line stores energy throughout its length; a failed rope, fitting or line of pull can sweep a large area. Painted snap-back zones cannot represent every real failure path.
A tidal window is the period when actual: A tidal window is the period when actual depth and operational restrictions permit passage. It depends on chart datum, forecast tide, squat, uncertainty and required UKC, which may change with speed and sea state.
A tug's useful force depends on thrust d: A tug's useful force depends on thrust direction, towline geometry and safe connection arrangements; rated bollard pull is not automatically available as lateral force at the ship's hull.
A VHF DSC distress alert on Channel 70 i: A VHF DSC distress alert on Channel 70 is a digital alert, not the subsequent spoken distress message. Radiotelephony distress traffic normally uses Channel 16 unless the situation and instructions dictate otherwise.
AC generators must meet prescribed volta: AC generators must meet prescribed voltage, frequency, phase sequence and phase-angle conditions for parallel connection. A closing error can produce damaging transients, torque and reverse-power events.
AC synchronising requires compatible vol: AC synchronising requires compatible voltage, frequency, phase sequence and phase angle before a generator breaker closes on a live bus. Out-of-phase closing may cause damaging torque and currents.
Advection fog forms when warm moist air: Advection fog forms when warm moist air moves over a colder surface, cooling below its dew point. Radiation fog typically arises through nocturnal cooling; sea visibility reductions need not coincide with precipitation.
AIS supplies transmitted identity and mo: AIS supplies transmitted identity and movement data but is not an independent collision avoidance sensor. GNSS input failures, erroneous static data and human edits can mislead the bridge.
Alarm Monitoring Systems observe sensor: Alarm Monitoring Systems observe sensor and control signals, but alarm acknowledgement is not fault rectification. A single high-level alarm may arise from real flooding, bad sensors, wiring or data transport.
An echo sounder measures acoustic travel: An echo sounder measures acoustic travel time to a reflecting surface; depth readout may be below the transducer or adjusted to a different reference. Draft, squat, offset, sound speed and seabed shape affect clearance.
An insulated-neutral ship distribution s: An insulated-neutral ship distribution system may remain in operation after a first earth fault while giving an insulation warning. A second fault on another phase can create dangerous fault current; the actual arrangement and protection must be identified from drawings.
An open-loop control output does not aut: An open-loop control output does not automatically correct for deviation, while closed-loop feedback compares a measured variable with a setpoint and adjusts the actuator. Sensor fault can defeat feedback despite normal controller operation.
Anchor watch combines movement monitorin: Anchor watch combines movement monitoring with depth, tide, weather, chain direction and nearby traffic. GNSS position alarms must account for vessel swing and the location of the antenna relative to the anchor.
Anchor watch uses planned swinging circl: Anchor watch uses planned swinging circle, actual chain length, fixing uncertainty and observed trends. Radius is not simply the number of shackles paid out: chain catenary, depth, hull length and weather affect the envelope.
Anchoring must consider holding ground,: Anchoring must consider holding ground, water depth, current, weather, planned swinging room and actual cable condition. The planned paid-out chain length is not the same as the vessel's distance from the anchor.
Annex III addresses harmful substances i: Annex III addresses harmful substances in packaged form, with marine pollutant identification and packaging, marking, documentation and stowage provisions implemented through the IMDG Code.
Apparent wind is the true wind vector re: Apparent wind is the true wind vector relative to the ship's movement through the relevant reference frame. Direction and reference source matter: ship heading, ground track and sensor corrections must not be confused.
Appraisal precedes detailed route design: Appraisal precedes detailed route design: chart coverage and quality, weather, tidal stream, services, machinery constraints and reporting requirements determine whether a proposed passage is feasible.
Azimuth is the true bearing of a celesti: Azimuth is the true bearing of a celestial or terrestrial object clockwise from true north, with corrections for observer position, time and ephemeris when celestial. It can help determine gyro or compass error when observation geometry is valid.
Ballast treatment and exchange are diffe: Ballast treatment and exchange are different compliance approaches. Operational decisions depend on the ship's approved Ballast Water Management Plan, treatment limitations, log entries and local port requirements.
Battery charging profiles depend on chem: Battery charging profiles depend on chemistry, ambient temperature, ventilation and control limits. Afloat and absorption charging must use compatible equipment; overcharge can generate heat/gas or shorten service life.
Battery thermal runaway can spread betwe: Battery thermal runaway can spread between cells while producing heat, flammable gases and toxic decomposition products. Chemistry-specific maker instructions and installed detection/suppression systems govern response.
Bay-row-tier slot codes locate container: Bay-row-tier slot codes locate containers in the stowage plan; load distribution, GM, stack-weight limits, lashing loads and verified gross mass are separate checks.
Beaufort is an observational wind-force: Beaufort is an observational wind-force scale; actual measured wind speed depends on averaging interval, instrument exposure and gust characteristics. Sea state is only a supporting observation, especially with swell or restricted fetch.
Biofouling and antifouling controls affe: Biofouling and antifouling controls affect invasive species and coatings, while ship recycling has separate hazardous-material and facility requirements. The IMO Hong Kong Convention entered into force on 26 June 2025; implementation depends on scope and administration.
Bridge Resource Management uses challeng: Bridge Resource Management uses challenge-response, explicit task allocation and shared situational awareness; alarms are prompts to investigate, not replacements for human cross-checks.
Buoyancy equals the weight of displaced: Buoyancy equals the weight of displaced water in equilibrium; displacement volume must be multiplied by the actual water density. Different seawater and dockwater densities give different immersed volumes for the same floating mass.
Cargo plans must satisfy local structura: Cargo plans must satisfy local structural loading, longitudinal strength, trim and intact stability as well as deck-space geometry. Two cargo plans with the same total mass can impose very different bending and shear forces.
Cargo restraint is designed for accelera: Cargo restraint is designed for accelerations produced by ship motions. A simple mass-times-acceleration estimate illustrates load, but selecting lashings also requires angles, friction, securing-point capacity and the ship's approved Cargo Securing Manual.
Cargo sweat and ship sweat arise from di: Cargo sweat and ship sweat arise from differing temperature and moisture conditions. The decision to ventilate depends on cargo properties, external air dew point and measured hold conditions, not simply on outside relative humidity.
Cascade control uses an outer controller: Cascade control uses an outer controller setting an inner-loop target; feedforward acts on a measured disturbance. The inner loop must remain reliable or the outer system may amplify an uncorrected process fault.
Chart course should be measured against: Chart course should be measured against the meridian/compass rose using the correct true reference; magnetically steered headings require separately applied variation and deviation. Bearing orientation from a chart is not automatically a corrected compass order.
Chart Datum is the reference surface fro: Chart Datum is the reference surface from which charted depths are normally measured. Tide heights above the applicable chart datum may be combined with chart depths for a static depth estimate, but LAT is not a synonym for every national chart datum.
CII is an operational carbon-intensity i: CII is an operational carbon-intensity indicator based on emissions and transport-work-related activity under a specified methodology. Lower total fuel consumption in isolation does not guarantee a better intensity indicator.
Closed-loop communication requires a pre: Closed-loop communication requires a precise instruction, correct read-back and explicit confirmation. The loop is especially important when similar machinery numbers or valve designations can be confused.
Closer isobar spacing in a fixed map sca: Closer isobar spacing in a fixed map scale often implies a stronger horizontal pressure gradient and stronger geostrophic wind, subject to latitude, surface friction and synoptic structure.
COLREG navigation lights have defined se: COLREG navigation lights have defined sectors, colours and minimum ranges based on vessel class and size. Geographical detection distance also depends on meteorological visibility and height of eye; a light's legal nominal range is not the distance at which every observer will see it.
COLREG Rule 13 obliges the overtaking ve: COLREG Rule 13 obliges the overtaking vessel to keep out of the way until finally past and clear. An approaching vessel more than 22.5° abaft another's beam is overtaking; doubt must be resolved conservatively.
COLREG Rule 15 identifies a crossing enc: COLREG Rule 15 identifies a crossing encounter between two power-driven vessels in sight. Risk assessment still depends on bearing trend, range, visual observation and all available sensors, not a single ARPA number.
COLREG Rule 6 requires safe speed approp: COLREG Rule 6 requires safe speed appropriate to conditions, including visibility, density of traffic, manoeuvrability, background light, weather and proximity of navigational hazards. There is no universally lawful fixed speed for restricted visibility.
COLREG Rules 5–8 apply across the routin: COLREG Rules 5–8 apply across the routine collision-avoidance decision chain: effective lookout, safe speed, risk assessment with all available means, and timely substantial action. Later encounter rules do not replace those fundamentals.

Control-loop tuning balances response ti: Control-loop tuning balances response time, stability, noise and actuator wear. A process that oscillates after maintenance may have altered sensor scaling or actuator dynamics, not merely inappropriate PID coefficients.
Corrective maintenance after breakdown p: Corrective maintenance after breakdown prioritises safe isolation, effect on essential services and systematic root-cause assessment. Restoring a machine to operation without checking the cause risks repeated or more severe failure.
Corrosion morphology can indicate differ: Corrosion morphology can indicate different mechanisms: galvanic corrosion depends on coupled dissimilar metals and electrolyte, while crevice corrosion may concentrate inside poorly ventilated gaps. Surface coating alone is not diagnosis.
Cospas-Sarsat 406 MHz alerts are process: Cospas-Sarsat 406 MHz alerts are processed through the satellite segment and ground network, then forwarded through LUT/MCC arrangements to responsible SAR coordination authorities. The beacon's GNSS position and independent satellite-derived location are not identical data sources.
Crane Safe Working Load and rigging capa: Crane Safe Working Load and rigging capacities apply under stated configurations and load paths. Sling angles increase tension as the angle to horizontal decreases, while dynamic effects and actual equipment limits remain critical.
Critical-equipment identification consid: Critical-equipment identification considers consequence of failure, available redundancy, detection and restoration time, not simply purchase price or physical size.
Cross-track error (XTE) is the lateral d: Cross-track error (XTE) is the lateral displacement from the active intended route leg, not a replacement for position uncertainty or danger-clearance limits. Turns, antenna offsets and chart accuracy also affect the interpretation.
Cumulonimbus clouds have strong vertical: Cumulonimbus clouds have strong vertical growth and may bring squalls, intense precipitation, lightning, gust fronts and sudden visibility change. The cloud's visible shape is evidence of convective activity but does not determine precise wind speed.
Cylinder-head maintenance requires engin: Cylinder-head maintenance requires engine cooling, pressure release, residual-fuel assessment, lifting plan and correct bolt preload sequence. A visual absence of leaks does not demonstrate safe lifting or correct reassembly.
Damage control requires monitored ingres: Damage control requires monitored ingress rates, boundary integrity and stability throughout the response. Pump operation, intentional transfers and counterflooding can affect free-surface and longitudinal stability in unexpected ways.
Dangerous goods transport combines accur: Dangerous goods transport combines accurate classification and declaration with package condition, documentation, stowage, segregation and emergency response. An identical UN number does not remove the need to check packing group and special provisions.
DC motor speed and torque characteristic: DC motor speed and torque characteristics depend on excitation and drive design. A series-excited DC motor can overspeed dangerously with loss of load; separately excited units depend on field integrity.
Departure is the east–west distance alon: Departure is the east–west distance along a local parallel, measured in NM, and is related to DLo via the cosine of latitude. It differs from east–west change in geodetic longitude, which is angular.
Direct-on-line induction motor starting: Direct-on-line induction motor starting draws significant inrush and starting torque, while star-delta starters and VFDs change the starting electrical and mechanical behaviour. Equipment compatibility and starting load torque matter.
Distress (MAYDAY), urgency (PAN PAN) and: Distress (MAYDAY), urgency (PAN PAN) and safety (SECURITE) communications represent different priorities and procedures. DSC alerting and follow-up radiotelephony use the relevant equipment and working channels; actual distress calls must never be used for drills.
DR advances a previous position by headi: DR advances a previous position by heading and speed through water; EP can additionally include estimated effects of current, wind and leeway. Their uncertainty grows with elapsed time without an independent fix.
Drydock preparation coordinates class su: Drydock preparation coordinates class survey items, hull inspections, sea valves, cathodic protection, anchors and shaft arrangements. Isolation planning must be established before exposure of sea-connected equipment.
Earth-leakage protective arrangements de: Earth-leakage protective arrangements detect residual current or insulation failure according to the installed earthing system. Correct device selection and testing depend on supply arrangement, load and protection zones.
ECDIS safety settings depend on the actu: ECDIS safety settings depend on the actual maximum draught, available chart depth and tide, squat, survey quality and company UKC policy. Safety contour and safety depth serve different presentation and alert functions.
ECDIS, radar and AIS are complementary b: ECDIS, radar and AIS are complementary but can share common heading, log and position errors. Independent cross-checks are based on distinct principles, not just different display brands.

Emergency logs should preserve observed: Emergency logs should preserve observed facts, communications and ordered actions with timestamps. Estimates and assumptions must be identified; accurate records support coordination and later investigation without delaying life-saving work.
Enclosed spaces can contain oxygen-defic: Enclosed spaces can contain oxygen-deficient, toxic or flammable atmospheres despite looking clean. An entry permit and gas test are control measures, not guarantees that the atmosphere will stay safe.
Enclosed-space casualty response require: Enclosed-space casualty response requires stopping a second uncontrolled entry, making a rescue plan and ensuring suitable atmosphere assessment and breathing protection. IMO revised enclosed-space recommendations stress additional permits for energy isolation and task-specific hazards.
Engine-room handover is a transfer of op: Engine-room handover is a transfer of operational risk awareness, not merely a signature. It should communicate plant status, isolations, alarms, planned work, temporary arrangements and escalation triggers.
ETA is driven by distance over ground di: ETA is driven by distance over ground divided by SOG, and through-water speed plus current may vary along the route. Fuel use depends on machinery loading and operating hours, so less time does not always imply proportional fuel savings.
Explosion-protected equipment suitabilit: Explosion-protected equipment suitability depends on the hazardous-area classification, gas/dust group, temperature class and protection concept. Damaged glands, incorrect spares and unapproved maintenance can invalidate protection.
Failure management must distinguish disp: Failure management must distinguish display, transducer, data bus and electrical supply faults. Backup navigation is only credible if equipment independence and competent procedures have been verified.
Fire integrity depends on A/B class divi: Fire integrity depends on A/B class divisions, penetrations, dampers, fire doors and detection zones as actually approved for the vessel. Fire ratings are not the same as a guarantee of unlimited fire resistance.
Fire-tube boilers route hot combustion p: Fire-tube boilers route hot combustion products through tubes surrounded by water, while water-tube designs circulate water/steam inside tubes exposed to hot gases. Both require correctly set water-level safeguards and blowdown plans.
Flash point is the lowest temperature at: Flash point is the lowest temperature at which a liquid produces sufficient vapour to ignite under a specified standard test; it is not the autoignition temperature and does not independently describe all storage hazards.
Flooding response combines watertight in: Flooding response combines watertight integrity, source identification, stability awareness, tank soundings and boundary integrity. Pump capacity can be exceeded by rising ingress even if a bilge alarm is acknowledged.
For a conventional synchronous alternato: For a conventional synchronous alternator, system frequency tracks shaft rotational speed and pole count; the governor regulates speed/real-power sharing while the AVR predominantly controls voltage/reactive-power behaviour.
GMDSS-approved mobile satellite terminal: GMDSS-approved mobile satellite terminals carry defined distress and safety functions within their recognised coverage. A vessel's commercial satellite internet access is not automatically a certified GMDSS alerting route.
GNSS geometric dilution of precision is: GNSS geometric dilution of precision is only one contributor to position uncertainty; orbit, timing, atmosphere, multipath, spoofing and equipment integrity also matter. Multiple displays sharing one sensor are not independent checks.
GNSS reliability can be affected by spoo: GNSS reliability can be affected by spoofing, jamming, multipath, antenna failure and shared sensor feeds. Multiple screens agreeing is not independent corroboration if they use the same receiver or antenna.
Grain cargo can shift in partly filled s: Grain cargo can shift in partly filled spaces and create heeling moments, so grain-stability requirements and approved loading conditions differ from ordinary solid bulk treatment.
Grounding creates local loads and potent: Grounding creates local loads and potential hull damage; refloating plans depend on verified bathymetry, tidal state, hull condition, stability and environmental consequences. Immediate full-astern power can worsen damage.
Gyrocompass and magnetic compass provide: Gyrocompass and magnetic compass provide distinct heading references. Gyro error changes with instrument state, speed/latitude influences, installation and sensor failures; it should not be treated as zero because it is electronic.
GZ is the horizontal lever between weigh: GZ is the horizontal lever between weight and buoyancy lines of action at a given angle of heel. Righting moment equals displacement weight multiplied by GZ under the corresponding units and assumptions.
HDOP describes how satellite geometry am: HDOP describes how satellite geometry amplifies horizontal ranging uncertainty. It is dimensionless and is not itself a position error in metres; receiver quality, interference, corrections and multipath also matter.
High-voltage marine electrical systems r: High-voltage marine electrical systems require authorised switching, isolation, testing for dead and earthing where specified. The correct safe state is established by the vessel's approved procedures and equipment ratings.
High-voltage shore connection must coord: High-voltage shore connection must coordinate voltage, frequency, phase sequence, grounding and protections between ship and terminal under an approved transfer plan. Galvanic and fault-current hazards are separate considerations.
Ho is observed celestial altitude after: Ho is observed celestial altitude after appropriate index, dip and astronomical corrections; Hc is computed altitude for an assumed position and ephemeris. The difference is an intercept in arcminutes and approximately nautical miles.
Hydrostatic gauge pressure increases wit: Hydrostatic gauge pressure increases with liquid density and vertical depth below a free surface. In a ventilated tank, p = ρgh applies to the column, not to vessel roll, acceleration or an air-pressurised space.

IMSBC Group A includes cargoes liable to: IMSBC Group A includes cargoes liable to liquefy or dynamically separate under relevant moisture conditions. Shipper documents and sampling arrangements matter; the master should not rely on the cargo looking dry.
In a head-on encounter between two power: In a head-on encounter between two power-driven vessels in sight and involving collision risk, Rule 14 requires each to alter course to starboard so that they pass port-to-port. Rules 5–8 still govern lookout, assessment and effective action.
In an ideal rectangular slack tank, tran: In an ideal rectangular slack tank, transverse free-surface moment scales with length times breadth cubed; actual tank shape, fill, baffles and liquid density modify the approved tabulated moment. Volume alone is insufficient.
In restricted visibility the officer mus: In restricted visibility the officer must assess risk with a proper lookout, safe speed and radar as applicable; COLREG Rule 19 is not a simple right-of-way chart copied from vessels in sight.
In restricted visibility, COLREG Rule 19: In restricted visibility, COLREG Rule 19 requires safe speed and risk assessment using all available means; fog signals are separate from radar target detection and must follow the vessel's actual navigational condition.
In the Northern Hemisphere the right sem: In the Northern Hemisphere the right semicircle relative to tropical cyclone motion is often the more dangerous due to rotational wind and storm translation. Forecast-track uncertainty, sea room and vessel speed make simple manoeuvre mnemonics insufficient.
In tropical cyclones, the eye may be com: In tropical cyclones, the eye may be comparatively calmer while the eyewall contains intense winds and heavy rain. A temporary lull does not imply that the storm has passed.
Initial metacentric height GM = KM minus: Initial metacentric height GM = KM minus KG at the loading draught. Free-surface correction lowers effective GM; small-angle positive GM alone cannot certify the entire righting-arm or damage-stability behaviour.
Insulation monitoring detects deteriorat: Insulation monitoring detects deterioration on certain marine insulated distribution systems. An alarm may occur without immediate breaker operation, so controlled investigation and electronic equipment protection are essential.
KG changes as a moment-weighted average: KG changes as a moment-weighted average when weights are added, shifted or removed. The final displacement changes with added mass, but not with movement of existing mass. Free-surface correction is considered separately.
Knot suitability depends on intended loa: Knot suitability depends on intended load, rope construction, bend radius, slip resistance and approved use. A correctly tied demonstration knot is not necessarily a certified cargo-lifting termination.
Latitude change and longitude change are: Latitude change and longitude change are signed angular differences. For local-plane navigation, departure ≈ DLo(minutes) × cos(mean latitude), and distance is the vector magnitude of DLat and departure.
Latitude is angular distance north or so: Latitude is angular distance north or south of the equator. In conventional nautical chart work, one minute of latitude approximately equals one nautical mile in the north–south direction, subject to Earth-ellipsoid refinements.
Laytime calculations depend on the speci: Laytime calculations depend on the specific charter party: notice of readiness, commencement clauses, exceptions, reversible time and agreed treatment of weather or port delays. Demurrage/despatch is contractual, not a universal hourly rule.
Leeway is the sideways drift relative to: Leeway is the sideways drift relative to the water caused by wind and hull form; its direction and magnitude vary with vessel, speed, exposure and loading. It is distinct from water-current set/drift.
Linear interpolation estimates an interm: Linear interpolation estimates an intermediate value from two adjacent tabulated entries only when the parameter is smooth over the interval. It is not valid across discontinuities, turnpoints or regulatory threshold changes.
Liquefied-gas cargo operations involve t: Liquefied-gas cargo operations involve temperature, pressure, cargo compatibility and hazardous-area controls. Cargo transfer procedures depend on tank type and the vessel's approved cargo system and terminal interface.
Liquid free surfaces shift the effective: Liquid free surfaces shift the effective centre of gravity during heel; their stability-booklet free-surface moment produces a virtual rise in G. The correction depends on tank geometry, filling state and the approved calculation basis.
LNG propulsion introduces cryogenic, fir: LNG propulsion introduces cryogenic, fire, vapour-management and fuel-gas system hazards that depend on certified design and the applicable IGF/IGC requirements. Gaseous leaks can create hazardous atmospheres even if visible liquid is absent.
Locally generated wind sea typically tra: Locally generated wind sea typically tracks the local wind field, whereas swell may travel long distances from a remote storm. Multiple wave trains can produce uncomfortable rolling despite moderate measured wind.
Longitude is the angle east or west of t: Longitude is the angle east or west of the prime meridian; distance along a parallel shrinks as latitude increases. Crossing 180° requires the shorter signed difference, not naive arithmetic on E and W labels.
Longitudinal weight movement creates a t: Longitudinal weight movement creates a trimming moment and changes trim, with the response governed by hydrostatic MCT 1 cm and LCF. A simple estimate does not provide the individual forward and aft draught changes.
Lost containers can create a navigation: Lost containers can create a navigation hazard and may also pose pollution or dangerous-goods risks. Immediate response must follow the ship's emergency and reporting procedures while preserving safe navigation and evidence.
Low-speed two-stroke marine diesel engin: Low-speed two-stroke marine diesel engines rely on efficient scavenge-air supply while exhaust gas is being displaced. One power stroke per revolution does not guarantee adequate fresh air at every load.
Machinery-space bilge water discharge re: Machinery-space bilge water discharge requires compliance with the vessel's approved oil-filtering equipment arrangements, 15-ppm monitoring where applicable and additional operational, area and port restrictions. A ppm readout alone is not authorisation.
Magnetic variation is the angular differ: Magnetic variation is the angular difference between true and magnetic north, varying by area and time; compass deviation is the error associated with the individual ship's compass heading.
Maintenance planning must consider hours: Maintenance planning must consider hours, calendar dates, maker requirements and operating duty; a late task may require additional risk controls and company authorisation. Deferral is not the same as completion.
Marine gas oil (MGO) is a distillate fue: Marine gas oil (MGO) is a distillate fuel class; marine diesel oil (MDO) terminology may refer to different distillate blends and grades. Density, viscosity, sulphur, ignition and compatibility are determined by the delivered fuel analysis and OEM limits, not the commercial label alone.
Marine LNG, methanol and other alternati: Marine LNG, methanol and other alternative fuels have different flammability, toxicity, cryogenic and atmosphere-management hazards. Equipment-specific procedures, IGF/IGC requirements where applicable and crew training govern transfers.
Marine radar estimates target range from: Marine radar estimates target range from the round-trip time of radio pulses. X- and S-band radars have different propagation/rain and resolution characteristics; echo strength also depends on target geometry, shadowing and sea clutter.
Maritime cyber risk can affect GNSS, ECD: Maritime cyber risk can affect GNSS, ECDIS updates, PMS and cargo systems; operational safety requires segregation, trusted change management and a fallback when electronic inputs are questionable.
Maritime Safety Information is selected: Maritime Safety Information is selected by coverage area, transmission schedules and message category. NAVTEX at 518 kHz normally carries English MSI; regional or national-language services may use different frequencies.
MARPOL Annex II covers noxious liquid su: MARPOL Annex II covers noxious liquid substances carried in bulk, with cargo categorisation and discharge requirements based on the IBC Code, a ship's Procedures and Arrangements Manual and approved records.
MARPOL Annex IV sewage requirements vary: MARPOL Annex IV sewage requirements vary by plant approval, comminution/disinfection status, distance from nearest land and special provisions. Retention is the safe option when discharge conditions are uncertain.
MARPOL Annex V imposes different disposa: MARPOL Annex V imposes different disposal requirements by garbage category, area and distance from land. Plastics are prohibited from discharge into the sea; garbage segregation and record keeping remain operational controls.
MARPOL Annex VI controls ship air pollut: MARPOL Annex VI controls ship air pollutants and energy-efficiency compliance. Sulphur limits are typically 0.50% m/m outside relevant SOx ECAs and 0.10% m/m inside; the Mediterranean became a SOx ECA on 1 May 2025.
MARPOL has six technical Annexes, regula: MARPOL has six technical Annexes, regulating oil, noxious liquid bulk cargo, packaged marine pollutants, sewage, garbage and air emissions. Applicable vessel certificates and discharge records differ by Annex and ship type.
