Mean latitude sailing approximates short: Mean latitude sailing approximates short or moderate passages using a mid-latitude cosine to convert longitude difference into departure. Its accuracy deteriorates with large changes in latitude, high-latitude geometry and long routes.
Meteorological and tidal currents may ch: Meteorological and tidal currents may change in both magnitude and direction. Set is the direction toward which current flows and drift is speed; the ship's COG/SOG differs from heading/log through water accordingly.
Methanol and ammonia require different t: Methanol and ammonia require different toxicity, flammability and materials/ventilation precautions; ship-specific approval, crew training and fuel-transfer instructions are critical. A generic 'alternative fuel' PPE set is insufficient.
MF/HF communications depend on propagati: MF/HF communications depend on propagation, chosen frequencies, antenna tuning, equipment status and the DSC watch arrangement. A nominal station range is not a reliable operational coverage guarantee.
Min-max inventory must cover lead time,: Min-max inventory must cover lead time, consumption, failure criticality and redundancy. A stock ledger can overstate usable spares when parts are expired, damaged or reserved for essential equipment.
Mooring hazards include stored elastic e: Mooring hazards include stored elastic energy, poor lead angles, mixed-line elasticity and damaged fittings. Snap-back paths vary with the actual line and hardware arrangement, not solely marked deck zones.
Motor protection must cover overload, st: Motor protection must cover overload, stalled rotor, phase loss, overheating and appropriate insulation condition. A protective trip records a symptom but needs diagnostic confirmation before restart.
Navigational warnings and permanent char: Navigational warnings and permanent chart corrections address different timescales. An ECDIS update status or a paper chart edition does not necessarily incorporate temporary hazards communicated by MSI.
NGA — American Practical Navigator (voya: NGA — American Practical Navigator (voyage planning context)
NOAA Ocean Prediction Center — Surface A: NOAA Ocean Prediction Center — Surface Analysis Charts
Nonlinear drives draw nonsinusoidal curr: Nonlinear drives draw nonsinusoidal currents that generate harmonic distortion and heating; total harmonic distortion (THD) describes their relative content, but absolute current and network impedance determine actual stress.
Oil analysis combines viscosity, wear pa: Oil analysis combines viscosity, wear particles, water content and contamination trends. One out-of-range sample may indicate a developing fault or a sampling error; trend and source verification matter.
On a Mercator navigation chart, distance: On a Mercator navigation chart, distance should be taken from the latitude scale near the route, where one minute of latitude is approximately one nautical mile; paper chart distortion varies with latitude.
Operational technology runs critical pro: Operational technology runs critical propulsion, power and cargo systems and requires controlled changes, validated firmware and secure vendor access. A legitimate-looking USB drive may introduce unsafe software.
Orifice differential-pressure meters inf: Orifice differential-pressure meters infer flow from pressure loss and fluid properties; Coriolis meters directly measure mass flow through oscillating tubes. Density, gas entrainment and calibration affect their accuracy.
Overcurrent protection must distinguish: Overcurrent protection must distinguish overload, short circuit and inrush, with protection selectivity coordinated across upstream/downstream breakers. Trip curves and interrupting ratings are equipment-specific.
Parallel indexing (PI) provides a radar-: Parallel indexing (PI) provides a radar-based monitoring line offset from the planned track to help maintain a safe passing distance from fixed charted features. It is not an independent position fix or a substitute for lookout.
Parametric rolling arises from periodic: Parametric rolling arises from periodic stability variation as waves encounter the hull. It can grow in head or following seas, depending on ship geometry, wave encounter period, natural rolling and speed, and threatens deck cargo securing.
Passage monitoring continuously verifies: Passage monitoring continuously verifies progress against the approved plan through independent fixes, guard zones, wheel-over confirmation and updates for actual traffic and environment.
Passage planning is a berth-to-berth pro: Passage planning is a berth-to-berth process of appraisal, planning, execution and monitoring. A route drawn through an ENC is only one part: safety depth/contour, squat, tidal margins, prohibited areas, MSI and contingency actions need evaluation.
Pilot transfer safety depends on approve: Pilot transfer safety depends on approved pilot ladder construction, correct rigging and securing, suitable deck lighting and trained supervision. A ladder's age or appearance alone does not establish safe condition.
Pilotage does not relieve the Master or: Pilotage does not relieve the Master or officer in charge of the navigational watch of their safety duties. The master–pilot exchange must cover vessel handling limits, communication, route, tugs and any agreed abort decisions.
PLC input/output modules translate field: PLC input/output modules translate field signals to controller logic and outputs. A valid CPU state does not prove every I/O signal is physically healthy, especially with open-circuit, stuck or inverted contacts.
Pollution prevention and fuel system dec: Pollution prevention and fuel system decision
Port State Control may examine whether c: Port State Control may examine whether charts/publications are adequate and updated, critical alarms are functional and crew are familiar with approved procedures. Demonstrated operation and actual records are stronger evidence than generic compliance claims.
Portable extinguishers must be matched t: Portable extinguishers must be matched to the fuel, fire class and electrical risk, and their availability does not replace alarm raising or escape-route assessment. Fire class terminology may vary by jurisdiction.
Position coordinates must identify latit: Position coordinates must identify latitude and longitude hemispheres together with the chart datum; a coordinate without N/S or E/W can produce a gross position error.
Position DOP (PDOP) reflects the three-d: Position DOP (PDOP) reflects the three-dimensional geometry of satellites in the positioning solution, while HDOP and VDOP reflect horizontal and vertical geometric effects. These are dimensionless multipliers, not position errors expressed in metres.
Post-collision response prioritises pers: Post-collision response prioritises personnel safety, watertight integrity, pollution control and accurate contact with authorities and neighbouring vessels. Liability arguments should not displace emergency checks.
PPE is the last layer after elimination,: PPE is the last layer after elimination, isolation and engineered safeguards. A Job Safety Analysis must consider dynamic energy sources, work interfaces, simultaneous operations and a stop-work trigger.
Practical machinery and shipboard risk a: Practical machinery and shipboard risk analysis
Prevention of harassment and violence re: Prevention of harassment and violence requires safe reporting, protection from retaliation and a fair, authorised investigation. Immediate safeguarding is distinct from the later determination of facts.
Preventive maintenance is scheduled from: Preventive maintenance is scheduled from maker guidance, equipment running hours, duty and criticality; a fixed calendar interval alone may be insufficient. Records must distinguish inspection, actual overhaul and deferred work.
Progressive flooding develops when initi: Progressive flooding develops when initial water ingress spreads through additional boundaries such as ducts, penetrations, doors and vents. Initial dry soundings do not rule out later loss of residual stability.
Proportional action reacts to present co: Proportional action reacts to present control error, integral action accumulates error over time, and derivative action reacts to its rate of change. Aggressive integral settings may cause windup when an actuator saturates.
Radar range measurements can establish a: Radar range measurements can establish an independent position fix when suitable land features and geometric intersection are available. Radar bearings may be less accurate than ranges depending on beamwidth and gyro-heading errors; chart and radar must use a consistent datum.
Refrigeration coefficient of performance: Refrigeration coefficient of performance relates heat removed at the evaporator to the work input over an agreed measurement boundary. It can exceed one because the system transports heat rather than converting work directly into cooling.
Reliability-centred maintenance chooses: Reliability-centred maintenance chooses run-to-failure, scheduled replacement, condition monitoring or functional testing based on credible failure modes and consequences. The cheapest immediate maintenance task may not minimise safety risk.
Remote quick-closing valves are intended: Remote quick-closing valves are intended to isolate fuel supply rapidly during a fire, typically without requiring entry to the affected space. Testing and resetting may have serious operational consequences.
Reserve GMDSS power must sustain require: Reserve GMDSS power must sustain required radio functions through approved supply arrangements and maintained batteries. Battery open-circuit voltage does not establish usable capacity under load.
Residual fuel catalytic fines are hard a: Residual fuel catalytic fines are hard aluminosilicate particles from refining, often assessed using aluminium plus silicon concentration. Separator efficiency, correct settling and cold/viscous fuel conditions determine abrasive particle exposure at engine injection.
Reverse osmosis drives seawater through: Reverse osmosis drives seawater through semipermeable membranes at pressure above osmotic pressure. Product-water quality, filter differential pressure and membrane limits must all be managed.
Rule 8 avoidance action should be positi: Rule 8 avoidance action should be positive, made in ample time and with due regard to good seamanship. A succession of small adjustments may obscure intent and fail to achieve adequate separation.
SAR communications separate alert receip: SAR communications separate alert receipt, on-scene coordination, search planning and rescue execution. The duty to assist and the authority of designated coordinators depend on the actual situation and governing plans.
Search and rescue communication distingu: Search and rescue communication distinguishes the MRCC, an appointed On-Scene Coordinator and individual assisting units. A first-arriving merchant ship must not assume unrestricted command authority.
Set indicates the direction the current: Set indicates the direction the current flows toward and drift its speed; vector additions should use ground-referenced units and identical time intervals. The heading/course-through-water vector must be kept distinct from COG.
Ship Security Assessment, approved Ship: Ship Security Assessment, approved Ship Security Plan and security levels determine authorised access and incident response. SSAS security alerts must not be confused with DSC or EPIRB distress broadcasts.
Significant wave height is a statistical: Significant wave height is a statistical measure, commonly the average of the highest third of waves, not a ceiling on individual waves. Wave period and direction strongly influence ship motions.
Since the 2024 GMDSS modernization, A3 i: Since the 2024 GMDSS modernization, A3 is defined relative to the coverage of a recognized mobile satellite service supported by the ship earth station fitted on board, outside A1 and A2. A4 is everything outside that ship's applicable A1/A2/A3 coverage.
SOLAS prescribes safety requirements and: SOLAS prescribes safety requirements and ISM implements a company and shipboard Safety Management System. Equipment presence, valid certificates and personnel competence each require separate evidence.
Standard Marine Communication Phrases mi: Standard Marine Communication Phrases minimise misunderstandings between VTS, pilots, bridge teams and ships. Course, speed, distance and urgency must be spoken and read back without ambiguity.
Standing orders and Master's night order: Standing orders and Master's night orders define bridge watch escalation triggers. Calling the Master is an additional safety measure and never transfers the watch officer's immediate duty to avoid danger.
Steering redundancy is meaningful only i: Steering redundancy is meaningful only if the backup control path, power availability, local control, communication and changeover procedures work together. The arrangement is installation-specific.
Surface analysis charts locate pressure: Surface analysis charts locate pressure centres, fronts, troughs and weather features at a stated valid time. A front's coloured symbols indicate front type and advance direction, while forecast and analysis charts have different time references.
Tank level devices use differing measure: Tank level devices use differing measurement principles (radar, differential pressure, float or capacitance). Fluid density, vapour and foaming can affect particular readings; independent high-level alarms must remain functional.
The 2008 IS Code combines mandatory and: The 2008 IS Code combines mandatory and recommended criteria, with ship-specific limitations and approved information. Positive initial GM is only one component of the intact stability assessment; the complete righting-arm curve matters.
The first law tracks energy crossing a d: The first law tracks energy crossing a defined system boundary as heat and work, plus changes in stored energy. An engine efficiency statement without a clear boundary can omit auxiliaries, exhaust and cooling losses.
The free-surface correction can be repre: The free-surface correction can be represented as a virtual rise of G for applicable tanks. Approved stability-booklet tables, density and actual slack-tank states must replace oversimplified constant corrections.
The GZ curve describes righting lever ov: The GZ curve describes righting lever over heel angle; the area under the curve represents dynamic stability only under the relevant assumptions. Peak GZ, range and downflooding angle require separate interpretation.
The GZ curve describes righting lever ve: The GZ curve describes righting lever versus heel for a specific loading condition. Its peak, positive range, integral and downflooding limits each convey different stability information; identical GM does not imply identical reserve stability.
The integral of GZ over heel angle repre: The integral of GZ over heel angle represents the quasi-static dynamic-stability area, expressed in m·rad. Displacement weight times this integral approximates work against heel; it is not a prediction of ship motions in random seas.
The live satellite image could not be lo: The live satellite image could not be loaded. Check the connection and press Refresh.
The modernized SOLAS IV GMDSS arrangemen: The modernized SOLAS IV GMDSS arrangements recognise applicable mobile satellite services beyond the older Inmarsat-only framing; the ship's certificate and approved equipment determine its actual A3 coverage. GMDSS and e-navigation have related but distinct purposes.
The planning phase converts appraisal ev: The planning phase converts appraisal evidence into waypoints and cross-track limits. The plan must account for manoeuvring radius, wheel-over positions, depth constraints, VTS reporting and contingency manoeuvres.
The radio log should distinguish equipme: The radio log should distinguish equipment checks, received warnings, tests, actual distress communications and periods when a required watch could not be maintained. Required entries depend on flag, sea area and the vessel's radio arrangements.
The rule of twelfths is a rough semidiur: The rule of twelfths is a rough semidiurnal-tide interpolation model, not a replacement for official port-specific tidal predictions, especially with mixed, diurnal or distorted tidal curves.
The Ship Security Alert System is a cove: The Ship Security Alert System is a covert security alerting means under ISPS/SOLAS XI-2 arrangements, not the radio distress alert route used by EPIRB or DSC. Recipients and test procedures are governed by the ship security plan.
Time Charter Equivalent is a comparative: Time Charter Equivalent is a comparative voyage earnings measure: voyage revenue less voyage-variable expenses, divided by voyage days on the chosen accounting basis. It is not necessarily the owner's net profit.
TMAS provides medical advice at sea; the: TMAS provides medical advice at sea; the bridge team must send precise observations and follow qualified medical direction. Initial emergency response should follow the vessel's trained first-aid protocols.
Towline tension reflects dynamic loads,: Towline tension reflects dynamic loads, vessel motions and relative movement, not only bollard-pull rating. Towing arrangements also require compatible fittings, release capability and agreed communications.
TPC is the approximate mass necessary to: TPC is the approximate mass necessary to change mean draught by 1 cm near the stated waterline, derived from waterplane area and water density. It varies with draught and loading condition.
Tropical cyclone avoidance should use fo: Tropical cyclone avoidance should use forecast motion, wind radii, track uncertainty, vessel capability and sea room. Historical 'dangerous semicircle' rules are only one decision aid, not a universal escape plan.
Ultrasonic thickness measurements requir: Ultrasonic thickness measurements require the correct material sound velocity, calibration and clean measurement locations. One apparent low reading can be caused by coating, coupling or surface geometry rather than true local corrosion.
Under-keel clearance is a dynamic margin: Under-keel clearance is a dynamic margin, not merely charted depth minus draught. Water level, vessel draught, heel, squat and uncertainty in soundings and position contribute to the passage decision.
Valve grinding and lash adjustment resto: Valve grinding and lash adjustment restore sealing and correct thermal clearances only within maker tolerances. Overgrinding can damage seat geometry or reduce valve margin, changing heat transfer and reliability.
VFDs vary motor electrical frequency and: VFDs vary motor electrical frequency and voltage/current under a drive control scheme, while mechanical limits and thermal cooling remain binding. Harmonics, electromagnetic interference and shaft-bearing effects require system assessment.
VLSFO compliance is not only a sulphur n: VLSFO compliance is not only a sulphur number. Different fuel blends may exhibit compatibility and stability problems; viscosity and heating arrangements affect service conditions.
VTS provides local traffic information a: VTS provides local traffic information and may issue instructions under local rules, but participation does not remove the Master's safe-navigation responsibilities or COLREG duties.
When vessels are not in sight of one ano: When vessels are not in sight of one another in or near restricted visibility, Rule 19 applies instead of the sight-based head-on and crossing allocation. Safe speed and assessment of radar contacts are central.
Worked navigation calculation and operat: Worked navigation calculation and operational check
Appraisal output: “Risk map of this pass: Appraisal output: “Risk map of this passage”.
What if the main engine fails?: What if the main engine fails?
VHF telsiz 156–174 MHz deniz bandında ça: The VHF radio works in the 156–174 MHz maritime band. The signal travels by line of sight, so the range depends on antenna height, and the ship-to-ship range is shorter than the range to coast stations with high antennas. On simplex channels only one station can talk at a time, so short standard phrases (SMCP) and channel discipline are essential.
VHF, köprüüstünün dış dünyayla en hızlı: VHF is the bridge's fastest link with the outside world: with the other ship when there is a risk of collision, with the pilot and VTS during berthing, and with the coast station and nearby ships in distress, first contact is usually made on this set. A wrong channel or a vague message can delay a correct decision.
SOLAS IV: DSC'li VHF telsiz tesisi (CH70: SOLAS IV: a VHF radio installation with DSC (DSC watch on Ch 70 and voice on Ch 16) is carried in all sea areas
SOLAS III/6: 500 GT ve üstü gemilerde en: SOLAS III/6: at least 3 GMDSS two-way VHF radiotelephones on ships of 500 GT and above, and at least 2 on ships of 300–500 GT
Telsiz trafiği ve testler GMDSS telsiz j: Radio traffic and tests are entered in the GMDSS radio log
CH16'yı uzun konuşmalar için kullanmak;: Using Ch 16 for long conversations and not moving to a working channel after first contact
Gemi adını, konumu ve niyeti net vermeme: Not giving the ship's name, position and intention clearly; agreeing COLREG manoeuvres by vague descriptions such as 'the red ship'
Squelch'i çok yüksek tutup zayıf çağrıla: Setting the squelch too high and missing weak calls
DSC, sesli haberleşmeden önce dijital bi: DSC sends a digital call before voice communication: Ch 70 on VHF and 2187.5 kHz on MF. The call carries the sender's MMSI, the priority (distress, urgency, safety, routine), the position and time, and the channel for the voice traffic that follows. A distress alert is repeated automatically by the set until it is acknowledged.
DSC sayesinde tek bir tuşla, konum ve te: With DSC, a single button sends an alert with the position and the nature of distress to every coast station and ship within range. The critical information goes out automatically even if the operator is under stress; a wrongly entered MMSI or an old position sends the rescue to the wrong place.
SOLAS IV: VHF-DSC tüm deniz alanlarında: SOLAS IV: VHF DSC is required in all sea areas; ships going beyond Sea Area A1 also carry at least MF DSC capability
Bayrak devletinin verdiği 9 haneli MMSI: The 9-digit MMSI assigned by the flag State must be entered correctly in the set
DSC fonksiyonları gerçek alarm gönderilm: DSC functions are tested without sending a real alert, using the set's test menu or a test call to a coast station
Yanlışlıkla gönderilen distress alarmını: Not cancelling a distress alert sent by mistake: the set is not switched off; the alert is stopped and its cancellation is announced on Ch 16 to 'All stations'
Konum GNSS'ten gelmediğinde eski konumla: Sending an alert with an old position when the position is not coming from the GNSS
Alınan distress alarmını DSC ile onaylam: Acknowledging a received distress alert by DSC; ships normally leave the acknowledgement to the coast station and, if necessary, reply by voice on Ch 16
ECDIS, resmî ENC verisini (S-57) GNSS ko: ECDIS combines official ENC data (S-57) with the GNSS position, gyro heading and log speed to show the ship's current position on the chart. Because it is a vector chart, depth contours and dangers are defined as objects, so the safety contour and look-ahead alarms can warn automatically of dangers on the route.
ECDIS bugün çoğu gemide birincil seyir a: On most ships today ECDIS is the primary means of navigation; the passage plan, position monitoring and shallow-water alarms are brought together on one screen. A wrongly set safety contour or a disabled alarm can take the ship into shallow water without a warning; misuse of ECDIS is among the main causes in many grounding reports.
SOLAS V/19: ECDIS, 500 GT ve üstü yolcu: SOLAS V/19: ECDIS became mandatory in phases between 2012 and 2018 for passenger ships of 500 GT and above, and for tankers and new cargo ships of 3000 GT and above
Yedek düzenleme: ikinci bağımsız ECDIS v: Back-up arrangement: a second independent ECDIS or an up-to-date folio of paper charts
STCW kapsamında genel ECDIS eğitimi ve g: Generic ECDIS training under STCW and type-specific training for the model fitted on board
Safety contour'u gemi draftına ve UKC'ye: Not setting the safety contour for the ship's draught and UKC; if the selected value is not in the ENC, the system uses the next deeper contour
Rota kontrolünü (route check) çalıştırma: Approving the route without running the route check or reading the warnings
Ekranı aşırı sadeleştirip seyir yardımcı: Decluttering the display too much and missing aids to navigation and caution areas; relying on an overscaled display
ENC güncellemelerini ve T&P bildirimleri: Sailing without applying the ENC updates and T&P notices
Radar kısa mikrodalga darbeleri gönderir: Radar transmits short microwave pulses; it finds the range from the time the echo takes to return and the bearing from the direction of the antenna. X-band (9 GHz, 3 cm) gives better resolution; S-band (3 GHz, 10 cm) is less affected by rain and sea clutter. ARPA calculates the target's course, speed, CPA and TCPA from successive measurements.
Radar; gece, sis ve yağmurda diğer gemil: At night, in fog and in rain, radar is the main sensor that shows other ships, the coastline and buoys, and it does not depend on the target: the echo appears even if the other ship's AIS is off. A correctly adjusted radar and systematic plotting are the basis of early and substantial action under the COLREGs.
SOLAS V/19: 300 GT ve üstü gemilerde 9 G: SOLAS V/19: a 9 GHz (X-band) radar on ships of 300 GT and above; on ships of 3000 GT and above, a second radar functionally independent of the first (3 GHz or a second 9 GHz)
SOLAS V/19: 500 GT ve üstü gemilerde oto: SOLAS V/19: ships of 500 GT and above have automatic target tracking (ATA or ARPA)
COLREG Kural 7: radar varsa uzun mesafe: COLREG Rule 7: if fitted, radar is used properly, including long-range scanning and systematic plotting
Çatışma önleme için ground stabilization: Using ground stabilization for collision avoidance; in a current the targets' aspect is shown wrongly, so sea stabilization is preferred for this purpose
Clutter'ı aşırı bastırıp küçük tekne ve: Suppressing clutter too much and removing small craft and buoys from the display
Yetersiz radar bilgisine (scanty radar i: Making decisions on scanty radar information, especially on a single observation
AIS bilgisini radarın yerine koymak; AIS: Treating AIS as a substitute for radar; targets that do not transmit AIS appear only on the radar
SAR, seyir engelleri, fener ve diğer sey: Passing SAR information, hazards to navigation, failures of lights and other aids to navigation and gale warnings to the bridge
NAVTEX, kıyı istasyonlarının sırayla, za: NAVTEX receives the broadcasts that coast stations transmit in turn on a time-sharing basis: international broadcasts in English on 518 kHz, national-language broadcasts on 490 kHz and broadcasts in tropical areas on 4209.5 kHz. Each message header consists of the station letter (B1), the message type (B2) and the serial number (B3B4); the receiver does not show the same message twice.
Batık, sönük fener, yeri değişmiş şamand: Information such as a wreck, an unlit light, a buoy out of position, a gale warning or a missing ship usually reaches the ship first through NAVTEX. This information is not yet on the chart; an officer of the watch who does not read the message remains unaware of the danger on the route.
SOLAS IV: NAVTEX hizmeti verilen bölgele: SOLAS IV: ships trading in areas where a NAVTEX service is provided carry a NAVTEX receiver
A (seyir uyarıları), B (meteorolojik uya: A (navigational warnings), B (meteorological warnings), D (SAR and piracy information) and L (additional navigational warnings) messages cannot be rejected by the receiver
Menzil tipik olarak kıyıdan yaklaşık 250: The range is typically about 250–400 nautical miles from the coast
Seyir bölgesindeki istasyonları (B1) seç: Forgetting to select the stations (B1) for the area of navigation; on entering a new area the receiver keeps listening to the old stations
Gelen uyarıyı okuyup rota üzerinde işare: Not plotting a received warning on the route or not passing it on at the watch handover
Kâğıt bitti veya hafıza doldu alarmını g: Ignoring the paper-out or memory-full alarm
AIS, VHF deniz bandında iki kanalda (AIS: AIS broadcasts data automatically on two channels in the VHF maritime band (AIS 1: 161.975 MHz, AIS 2: 162.025 MHz). Class A units share time slots by SOTDMA; dynamic data is sent every few seconds depending on speed and turning, every 3 minutes at anchor, and static and voyage data every 6 minutes. The position and speed come from the ship's own GNSS.
AIS, hedefin adını, MMSI'sini ve niyetin: AIS shows the target's name, MMSI and intentions (destination, navigational status); it makes bridge-to-bridge communication easier and can even show ships in the radar shadow. However, only ships that transmit are visible and the data depends on the other ship's input; AIS therefore supplements radar and does not replace it.
SOLAS V/19: uluslararası sefer yapan 300: SOLAS V/19: ships of 300 GT and above on international voyages, cargo ships of 500 GT and above not on international voyages, and all passenger ships carry AIS
Performans standardı: IMO MSC.74(69) Ek: Performance standard: IMO MSC.74(69) Annex 3; guidelines for onboard use: IMO A.1106(29)
AIS sürekli çalışır durumda tutulur; yal: AIS is kept in operation at all times; it is switched off only if the Master considers it necessary for the safety of the ship (e.g. piracy risk), and this is recorded
Seyir durumunu (navigational status) gün: Not updating the navigational status: transmitting 'at anchor' while the ship is under way
Draft, varış limanı ve ETA'yı sefer başı: Not updating the draught, destination and ETA at the start of the voyage
AIS'in CPA/TCPA değerine tek başına güve: Relying on the AIS CPA/TCPA alone; the other ship's position depends on its GNSS and its heading on its gyro connection, and either may be wrong
Her teknenin AIS yayını yaptığını varsay: Assuming that every craft transmits AIS
Gyro pusula, hızla dönen bir rotorun Dün: The gyrocompass works by a fast-spinning rotor that seeks true north through its interaction with the Earth's rotation and gravity. As it is not affected by the magnetic field it has no deviation or variation, but there may be a speed and latitude error and a small constant gyro error. After starting, it takes several hours to settle on north.
Radar, ECDIS, ARPA, AIS ve otopilot head: Radar, ECDIS, ARPA, AIS and the autopilot take their heading from the gyro. An error of a few degrees in the gyro shifts the radar overlay, makes ARPA calculate a wrong CPA and lets the autopilot take the ship quietly off course; the magnetic compass is the last independent heading reference when the power fails.
SOLAS V/19: tüm gemilerde güç kaynağı ge: SOLAS V/19: all ships have a magnetic compass that needs no power supply and a means of taking bearings
SOLAS V/19: 500 GT ve üstü gemilerde gyr: SOLAS V/19: ships of 500 GT and above have a gyrocompass and a heading indicator visible from the emergency steering position
STCW A-VIII/2: pusula hataları en az var: STCW A-VIII/2: compass errors are determined at least once a watch and, when possible, after any major alteration of course
Gyroya enlem ve sürat girdisi elle veril: Not updating the latitude and speed inputs to the gyro when they are entered manually
Güç kesintisinden sonra repeater'ları an: Using the repeaters after a power failure without aligning them with the master gyro
Gyro hatasını kontrol etmeden kerterize: Relying on bearings and parallel indexing without checking the gyro error
Otopilot (heading control system), gyrod: The autopilot (heading control system) measures the difference between the heading from the gyro and the set course and orders a corrective rudder angle from the steering gear. The rudder (gain), counter rudder and yaw (weather) settings determine how firmly and how often the rudder is used. In track control mode it also corrects the XTD against the route from ECDIS and makes the turns at the waypoints.
Otopilot uzun açık deniz seyrinde dümenc: The autopilot relieves the helmsman on long ocean passages and saves fuel; but in many collisions and groundings the officer of the watch left the ship on autopilot and changed to hand steering too late. Every officer must know the modes, the alarms and the steps for changing to hand steering by heart.
SOLAS V/24: yoğun trafikte, kısıtlı görü: SOLAS V/24: when automatic steering is used in areas of high traffic density, in restricted visibility and in other hazardous navigational situations, it must be possible to establish manual steering immediately and a qualified helmsperson must be available
SOLAS V/24: uzun süre otomatik dümen kul: SOLAS V/24: manual steering is tested after prolonged use of automatic steering and before entering areas where navigation demands special caution
SOLAS V/26: kalkıştan önceki 12 saat içi: SOLAS V/26: the steering gear is tested within 12 hours before departure; emergency steering drills are held at least once every three months
Performans standartları: heading control: Performance standards: IMO MSC.64(67) Annex 3 for heading control and IMO MSC.74(69) Annex 2 for track control
Pilot alırken veya bırakırken, dar geçit: Staying on autopilot when embarking or disembarking the pilot, in a narrow channel or in heavy traffic
El dümenine geçişte override/take-over d: Not knowing where the override/take-over button is and the order of the selector switch when changing to hand steering
Ağır havada yaw (weather) ayarını artırm: Not increasing the yaw (weather) setting in heavy weather, so that the steering gear works continuously
Terminalin oturum (login) durumunu ve ba: Check daily the terminal's login status and the ocean-region satellite it is logged in to
Inmarsat-C terminali, yer sabit (geostat: The Inmarsat-C terminal sends and receives messages through geostationary satellites on a store-and-forward basis. The EGC (Enhanced Group Call) receiver automatically receives the SafetyNET maritime safety information broadcast for the NAVAREA/METAREA where the ship is. Geostationary satellites do not cover areas beyond about 70° north and south latitude.
Açık okyanusta NAVTEX menzili bittiğinde: On the open ocean, when the ship is out of NAVTEX range, storm, ice, piracy and SAR information reaches it through SafetyNET. In Sea Area A3 the same terminal is also the main route for distress alerting and messaging between the ship and the rescue coordination centre.
SOLAS IV: A3 deniz alanında sefer yapan: SOLAS IV: ships trading in Sea Area A3 must be able to send a distress alert through a ship earth station of a recognized mobile satellite service or by MF/HF DSC
NAVTEX kapsaması dışında MSI almak için: An EGC (SafetyNET) receiver is needed to receive MSI outside NAVTEX coverage
IMO, 2018'de Iridium'u da GMDSS'te tanın: In 2018 IMO also recognized Iridium as a satellite service in the GMDSS
SOLAS IV/18: tehlike alarmına konum otom: SOLAS IV/18: if the position is not entered into the distress alert automatically, it is updated manually at intervals not exceeding 4 hours while under way
Seyir bölgesi değiştiğinde NAVAREA/METAR: Not updating the NAVAREA/METAREA and coastal warning areas when the area of navigation changes
EGC mesaj listesini veya yazıcı kâğıdını: Taking over the watch without checking the EGC message list or the printer paper
Distress düğmesine test amacıyla basmak;: Pressing the distress button for a test; tests are carried out only with the set's test procedure
Pilotaj, demirleme ve dar geçitlerde der: Entering the depths in the deck logbook at regular intervals during pilotage, anchoring and in narrow channels
Ölçüm aralığını (range) beklenen derinli: Select the range for the expected depth; in deep water a second-trace echo can give a misleading shallow reading
Derinlik trendinin ECDIS ve conning ekra: Display of the depth trend on the ECDIS and the conning display
İskandil, transdüserden suya akustik bir: The echo sounder sends an acoustic pulse into the water from the transducer and measures the time the echo takes to return from the seabed; the depth is calculated by taking the speed of sound in sea water as about 1500 m/s. The measured value is the depth below the transducer; to show the depth below the keel or the waterline, the offset must be entered correctly.
Karaya oturmaya giden zincirin son halka: At the last link of the chain that leads to a grounding, the echo sounder is the only device that tells whether the charted depth is really there. A correct offset and a well-set shallow-water alarm show an error in the ECDIS or in the position while there is still time.
SOLAS V/19: 300 GT ve üstü gemiler ile t: SOLAS V/19: ships of 300 GT and above and all passenger ships have an echo-sounding device
Performans standardı: IMO MSC.74(69) Ek: Performance standard: IMO MSC.74(69) Annex 4; the device must be able to show the depth record of the last 12 hours
Yükleme veya tahliyeden sonra draft deği: Not updating the offset when the draught changes after loading or discharging
Ekrandaki derinliğin transdüserin, omurg: Not knowing whether the displayed depth is measured below the transducer, the keel or the waterline
Hava kabarcığı, balık sürüsü veya termok: Taking false echoes from air bubbles, schools of fish or a thermocline for the real seabed
Kayda girmeyen veya arızalı girdileri VD: Identifying and recording inputs that are not recorded or are faulty from the VDR alarm panel
Kaza veya ciddi bir olaydan sonra kaydı: After an accident or serious incident, save/back up the record at once; do not switch off the unit or delete data
Köprüüstü mikrofonlarının çalıştığını ve: Verify with the APT and routine checks that the bridge microphones work and the recording is intelligible
Kaza soruşturmasında VDR verileri bayrak: In a casualty investigation the VDR data is used by the flag State's investigating body
VDR; köprüüstü mikrofonlarını, VHF konuş: The VDR continuously records the bridge microphones, VHF communications, radar and ECDIS displays, position, speed, heading, rudder and engine orders and responses, depth, wind, AIS and the main alarms on a common time stamp. Recording is cyclic: old data is overwritten by new data. The data is stored in a fixed capsule that resists impact, fire and pressure and, on newer VDRs, also in a float-free capsule that floats free if the ship sinks.
Kaza sonrası 'ne oldu?' sorusunun tarafs: The VDR holds the impartial answer to 'what happened?' after an accident: investigators replay the bridge conversations, the displays and the orders second by second. A VDR that does not work, or whose record is not saved, means the lessons are lost and can lead to consequences against the ship and the officer.
SOLAS V/20: yolcu gemileri ile 3000 GT v: SOLAS V/20: passenger ships and other ships of 3000 GT and above carry a VDR; an S-VDR was accepted for existing cargo ships
SOLAS V/18.8: VDR'nin yıllık performans: SOLAS V/18.8: the VDR's annual performance test (APT) is carried out by an approved service provider
Performans standardı: 1 Temmuz 2014 ve s: Performance standard: IMO MSC.333(90) for VDRs installed on or after 1 July 2014
Sabit kapsüldeki sualtı yer belirleme ve: The expiry date of the battery of the underwater locating beacon (ULB) on the fixed capsule is tracked
Olaydan sonra kaydı yedeklemeyi unutmak;: Forgetting to save the record after an incident; cyclic recording overwrites the critical minutes
Sürekli tekrarlayan VDR arıza alarmını s: Silencing a recurring VDR fault alarm without investigating the cause
Köprüüstü mikrofonlarının önünü kapatmak: Covering the bridge microphones or making the recording unintelligible with a loud radio or music
Uzak alarm noktalarının (kaptan ve zabit: Periodic test of the remote alarm points (Master's and officers' cabins)
Acil çağrı (emergency call) düğmesiyle k: Using the emergency call button to call the Master or the back-up officer to the bridge at once
Reset düğmelerinin vardiya zabitinin nor: Checking that the reset buttons can be reached from the officer of the watch's normal lookout positions
Otomatik modda, heading veya track contr: In automatic mode, the BNWAS starts by itself when heading or track control (autopilot) is engaged
BNWAS, vardiya zabitinin belirli bir sür: The BNWAS confirms the officer of the watch is alert when a reset button is pressed or movement is detected within a set period (dormant period, 3–12 minutes). If there is no confirmation, the alarm escalates: first a visual indication on the bridge, after 15 seconds an audible alarm on the bridge, then a remote alarm at the location of the Master or the back-up officer, and later an alarm at the locations of other crew members.
Gece vardiyasında uyuyakalan veya aniden: A single officer who falls asleep or is suddenly taken ill on the night watch can take the ship aground or into another ship within minutes. The BNWAS detects this and alerts the Master and the crew in turn; it is the last safety net of a one-person bridge watch.
SOLAS V/19: 150 GT ve üstü gemiler ile t: SOLAS V/19: ships of 150 GT and above and all passenger ships have a BNWAS (phased in from 2011 to 2014)
SOLAS V/19: BNWAS, gemi denizde seyirdey: SOLAS V/19: the BNWAS is in operation whenever the ship is under way at sea
Çalışma modu ve süre ayarı yalnız kaptan: The operating mode and the time setting can be changed only with a key or password that only the Master can access
Reset düğmesine ağırlık koymak veya hare: Putting a weight on the reset button or rigging something that keeps triggering the motion sensor
Denizde BNWAS'ı kapalı modda bırakmak: Leaving the BNWAS in off mode at sea
Uzak alarmları test etmeyip yalnız köprü: Testing only the bridge alarm and not the remote alarms
